title: How a Scaffold Keeps Signals on Route

scenes.tts: The first film used Grb2 to route a receptor signal toward Ras. But what if two pathways share the same kinase? Follow the same colors as one orange kinase faces two possible purple outputs.
scenes.caption: The first film used Grb2 to route a receptor signal toward Ras. But what if two pathways share the same kinase? Follow the same colors as one orange kinase faces two possible purple outputs.
scenes.visual: Reuse the first film's COLOR MAP exactly: input blue; organizer green; enzyme orange; output purple; phosphate gold; inactive labels gray. Fus3 is a kinase: draw it orange like Ste11 and Ste7, with a purple ring marking it as the mating output. Transform the first film's receptor–Grb2–Sos cluster into a fork. One orange kinase moves toward two purple output blocks under different blue inputs. Mark every block diagram 'schematic'.
scenes.narration: The first film used Grb2 to route a receptor signal toward Ras. But what if two pathways share the same kinase? Follow the same colors as one orange kinase faces two possible purple outputs.

scenes.visual: Curve the fork into the title 'How a Scaffold Keeps Signals on Route'. Keep the shared orange kinase visible below the title. Fade the title while the fork straightens into a pathway.

scenes.tts: Yeast mating uses a kinase route ending in Fus3. Some upstream kinases also serve other responses. A pheromone input must reach the mating output without making the cell follow every route that shares a part.
scenes.caption: Yeast mating uses a kinase route ending in Fus3. Some upstream kinases also serve other responses. A pheromone input must reach the mating output without making the cell follow every route that shares a part.
scenes.visual: A blue pheromone input enters from left. Orange Ste11 and Ste7 blocks occupy the center. An orange Fus3 kinase with a purple output ring sits right, with two dim alternative branches above and below. Animate a pulse that hesitates at the shared orange blocks.
scenes.narration: Yeast mating uses a kinase route ending in Fus3. Some upstream kinases also serve other responses. A pheromone input must reach the mating output without making the cell follow every route that shares a part.

scenes.tts: A shared kinase does not carry a label saying which response should follow. Its meaning depends on the partners around it. The cell therefore needs an organizer that assembles the mating route under the mating input.
scenes.caption: A shared kinase does not carry a label saying which response should follow. Its meaning depends on the partners around it. The cell therefore needs an organizer that assembles the mating route under the mating input.
scenes.visual: Remove route labels from the shared orange kinase and rotate it slowly at the fork. Bring in a green organizer outline around the mating branch only. The blue pheromone input pulls that outline toward the membrane while other branches stay neutral.
scenes.narration: A shared kinase does not carry a label saying which response should follow. Its meaning depends on the partners around it. The cell therefore needs an organizer that assembles the mating route under the mating input.

scenes.tts: Ste5 is a green scaffold with no enzyme activity. Different regions bind Ste11, Ste7 and Fus3, so one Ste5 can hold all three. This assembly can make productive encounters more likely.
scenes.caption: Ste5 is a green scaffold with no enzyme activity. Different regions bind Ste11, Ste7 and Fus3, so one Ste5 can hold all three. This assembly can make productive encounters more likely.
scenes.visual: Grow one large green Ste5 rail across the frame. Orange Ste11, orange Ste7 and purple-ringed orange Fus3 slide onto three distinct shaped slots; the slots are spaced irregularly and must not imply that binding order follows cascade order. A blue input pulse moves through the assembly. Keep the alternative branches dim but visible.
scenes.narration: Ste5 is a green scaffold with no enzyme activity. Different regions bind Ste11, Ste7 and Fus3, so one Ste5 can hold all three. This assembly can make productive encounters more likely.

scenes.tts: Within the assembled route, Ste11 activates Ste7, and Ste7 activates Fus3. Fus3 helps prepare the cell for mating. The scaffold does not perform those kinase reactions. It organizes the proteins that do.
scenes.caption: Within the assembled route, Ste11 activates Ste7, and Ste7 activates Fus3. Fus3 helps prepare the cell for mating. The scaffold does not perform those kinase reactions. It organizes the proteins that do.
scenes.visual: Pulse from orange Ste11 to orange Ste7, then into purple-ringed orange Fus3. Each block brightens only when the pulse arrives. Keep the green Ste5 rail steady and add a small 'organizes' label, while brief kinase flashes occur between the blocks.
scenes.narration: Within the assembled route, Ste11 activates Ste7, and Ste7 activates Fus3. Fus3 helps prepare the cell for mating. The scaffold does not perform those kinase reactions. It organizes the proteins that do.

scenes.tts: Proximity is only the first model. Ste5 responds to pheromone-linked recruitment at the membrane. Its shape opens there. A Ste5 domain also helps Ste7 activate Fus3, which is otherwise a poor substrate.
scenes.caption: Proximity is only the first model. Ste5 responds to pheromone-linked recruitment at the membrane. Its shape opens there. A Ste5 domain also helps Ste7 activate Fus3, which is otherwise a poor substrate.
scenes.visual: Fold the green Ste5 rail into a closed U shape away from a gray membrane. A blue pheromone cue recruits it upward; the rail opens. Transform one green slot into a gate that aligns orange Ste7 with purple-ringed orange Fus3.
scenes.narration: Proximity is only the first model. Ste5 responds to pheromone-linked recruitment at the membrane. Its shape opens there. A Ste5 domain also helps Ste7 activate Fus3, which is otherwise a poor substrate.

scenes.tts: The scaffold therefore helps select an output. It controls partners, place and activation, rather than locking every shared kinase away. The same shared parts can behave differently inside a different organized context.
scenes.caption: The scaffold therefore helps select an output. It controls partners, place and activation, rather than locking every shared kinase away. The same shared parts can behave differently inside a different organized context.
scenes.visual: Send the blue pulse through membrane-open Ste5 to light the purple ring on Fus3. Leave the alternative purple outputs dim, without crossing them out. Then lift the shared orange blocks briefly and settle them into a different faint organizer to show context changing.
scenes.narration: The scaffold therefore helps select an output. It controls partners, place and activation, rather than locking every shared kinase away. The same shared parts can behave differently inside a different organized context.

scenes.tts: The filament-growth route uses Ste11 and Ste7 but ends at Kss1. One salt-stress branch uses Ste11, then a different middle kinase, and ends at Hog1. Only the mating route has Ste5, so only the mating route switches on Fus3.
scenes.caption: The filament-growth route uses Ste11 and Ste7 but ends at Kss1. One salt-stress branch uses Ste11, then a different middle kinase, and ends at Hog1. Only the mating route has Ste5, so only the mating route switches on Fus3.
scenes.visual: Draw two faint alternative routes with no green scaffold. Route one: orange Ste11 to orange Ste7 to a separate orange kinase labelled 'Kss1'. Route two: a copy of orange Ste11 only, then an unlabelled orange middle kinase, then an orange kinase labelled 'Hog1'; Ste7 must not appear in this route. Keep purple-ringed Fus3 exclusively on open green Ste5. Animate a blue mating pulse through Ste5, then separate neutral pulses through the alternative routes, without marking either as rejected.
scenes.narration: The filament-growth route uses Ste11 and Ste7 but ends at Kss1. One salt-stress branch uses Ste11, then a different middle kinase, and ends at Hog1. Only the mating route has Ste5, so only the mating route switches on Fus3.

scenes.tts: Suppose the cell keeps adding empty Ste5 scaffolds. Must the number of complete kinase assemblies keep rising? Watch where each kinase might land, then make your prediction.
scenes.caption: Suppose the cell keeps adding empty Ste5 scaffolds. Must the number of complete kinase assemblies keep rising? Watch where each kinase might land, then make your prediction.
scenes.visual: Place one complete green scaffold assembly at center. Duplicate empty green scaffolds around it while keeping the same three kinase blocks floating above. Show the question at top. Do not move any kinase onto a scaffold yet.
scenes.narration: Suppose the cell keeps adding empty Ste5 scaffolds. Must the number of complete kinase assemblies keep rising? Watch where each kinase might land, then make your prediction.

scenes.visual: Keep the question visible. Let the empty scaffolds drift slightly apart and the three kinase blocks hover. Reveal no distribution or output during the thinking pause.

scenes.tts: No. In the simplest model, all three kinases must share one scaffold to signal. With scaffold in excess, they spread across different scaffold molecules. Fewer scaffolds are complete, so predicted output falls. This model effect is called combinatorial inhibition.
scenes.caption: No. In the simplest model, all three kinases must share one scaffold to signal. With scaffold in excess, they spread across different scaffold molecules. Fewer scaffolds are complete, so predicted output falls. This model effect is called combinatorial inhibition.
scenes.visual: Distribute Ste11, Ste7 and Fus3 onto separate green scaffolds. The complete central assembly dissolves into incomplete ones. A small output gauge falls; label it 'model, schematic'. Do not show a numeric curve or uncomputed values.
scenes.narration: No. In the simplest model, all three kinases must share one scaffold to signal. With scaffold in excess, they spread across different scaffold molecules. Fewer scaffolds are complete, so predicted output falls. This model effect is called combinatorial inhibition.

scenes.tts: Experiments support both layers. Ste5 binds the mating kinases on different regions. Later work showed that a Ste5 domain makes Fus3 easier for Ste7 to activate. Assembly and selective activation work together.
scenes.caption: Experiments support both layers. Ste5 binds the mating kinases on different regions. Later work showed that a Ste5 domain makes Fus3 easier for Ste7 to activate. Assembly and selective activation work together.
scenes.visual: Reassemble one complete Ste5 complex. First highlight the three distinct binding slots. Then animate the green gate aligning orange Ste7 with purple-ringed orange Fus3. Two check marks appear beside labels 'assembly' and 'selective activation'; keep them moving into one combined bracket.
scenes.narration: Experiments support both layers. Ste5 binds the mating kinases on different regions. Later work showed that a Ste5 domain makes Fus3 easier for Ste7 to activate. Assembly and selective activation work together.

scenes.tts: Return to the fork. A shared kinase does not choose an output alone. The organizer around it changes which partners meet, where the complex forms and whether the last step can proceed.
scenes.caption: Return to the fork. A shared kinase does not choose an output alone. The organizer around it changes which partners meet, where the complex forms and whether the last step can proceed.
scenes.visual: Transform the Ste5 rail back into the opening fork. Enclose only the mating route with the green organizer and place it at the membrane. The blue input pulse reaches purple-ringed Fus3. Other outputs remain neutral, not rejected or crossed out.
scenes.narration: Return to the fork. A shared kinase does not choose an output alone. The organizer around it changes which partners meet, where the complex forms and whether the last step can proceed.

scenes.visual: Show one line only, centered and large: 'Scaffolds route shared parts by controlling partners, place and activation.' No title, logo, subtitle, URL or smaller line. Let a faint green organizer line draw itself beneath the sentence without adding text.
